hyps.why: At tiny learning rates the network is undertrained after 243 epochs, so increasing the step size yields large gains.
At already-large learning rates Adam diverges or stalls, so pushing higher hurts accuracy.
Reducing an overly large learning rate escapes the divergent regime and recovers accuracy.
Lowering an already tiny learning rate worsens undertraining.
Small batches already give many noisy updates, so a larger step size amplifies instability.
With a tiny learning rate, fewer updates per epoch from larger batches exacerbates undertraining.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, partially stabilizing training at high learning rates.
Near alpha=1 the L2 penalty dominates the loss and further increases cause strong underfitting.
At negligible alpha, increasing it has essentially no effect, unlike the harmful effect at larger alpha.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to unstable training under large learning rates.
